findings.description: The publicly served /runtime-config.js (loaded on the login page, no sign-in needed) embeds the customer test account credentials as a base64 string in window.__SL_RUNTIME__.a. Anyone who fetches the file can decode it to the username and password.
repro: Base64-decode the value of the 'a' field: it decodes to customer-acbb:[redacted], the customer sign-in.

findings.description: Document responses carry no hardening headers: no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options (or frame-ancestors) or Strict-Transport-Security. The nginx Server header also exposes its version (nginx/1.29.8).
repro: Observe that the response headers contain only Server, Date, Content-Type, Content-Length, Last-Modified, Connection, ETag and Accept-Ranges.

findings.description: On the order-complete page the 'Generate PDF order' button label wraps onto two lines inside a narrower box than the adjacent 'Back Home' button, so the two action buttons look unequal in size and text alignment.
repro: Sign in as customer-acbb, add any product to the cart, and complete checkout (Checkout, fill the form, Continue, Finish).
On the Checkout: Complete! page, look at the two buttons below the message.

notes: Tested as customer-acbb in Chromium at 1280px and 375px. Covered: login (empty, wrong password, unknown user), the six-product inventory, all four sort orders (names and prices correct), add/remove from list, detail and cart with badge persistence across reload, cart contents, checkout validation (first, last and postal code required), overview totals (item total, 8% tax, total all verified arithmetically for 1, 2 and 6 items), order completion (cart cleared, badge cleared), the generated order PDF (totals match the screen), logged-out redirects on all protected routes, the burger menu, Reset App State, the Dynamic Catalog Lazy Load (infinite scroll works), Spinner and Slider pages, mobile overflow (none) and a basic a11y scan (images, buttons, inputs and links all named). The ITEM NOT FOUND page for unknown product ids (dog image, '$√-1', dial-an-operator copy) looks like the deliberate Swag Labs easter egg, so it was not reported. Footer Terms of Service and Privacy Policy are plain text, which I took as intended. Not tested: other user accounts (only one was supplied), payment and shipping validation beyond the fields shown, and deeper a11y (contrast, keyboard focus order) and load testing beyond single-page timings.
